name: Apigee
description: Apigee is Google Cloud's API management platform that helps organizations design, secure, publish, and analyze APIs at scale.
best_for: Per the page, Apigee is for enterprise organizations managing multiple APIs, API developers, API teams needing governance/security, and businesses exposing services securely to partners and customers.
features: Visual API design and development/prototyping tools
API security: threat protection, OAuth 2.0, traffic management
Real-time API analytics and performance monitoring
Developer Portal for publishing docs and onboarding
Policy enforcement: rate limiting, quota management, governance

alternatives.name: Kong
alternatives.description: Offers API gateway and management products directly comparable to Apigee's design/security/governance capabilities, positioned around AI connectivity and multi-cloud deployment.
alternatives.best_for: Teams wanting a cloud-agnostic API gateway with AI-agent-specific tooling.

alternatives.name: RapidAPI
alternatives.description: A public API marketplace/hub for discovering and consuming APIs.
alternatives.best_for: Developers wanting quick discovery/testing of external APIs rather than full enterprise governance tooling.

pricing.starting_price: Pay as you go; cost depends on active environments per region, API calls, proxy deployment units, and network usage

tiers.name: Pay as you go
tiers.notes: Metered across active environment type and region, API calls to deployed proxies, proxy deployment units per hour and region, and applicable network charges.

tiers.name: Subscription
tiers.notes: Contract pricing is available through Google Cloud sales; published pay-as-you-go documentation does not provide one universal subscription price.

tiers.name: Evaluation organization
tiers.notes: Time-limited evaluation for new Apigee customers. It does not support production workloads and is not covered by Google support terms.

pros: Pay-as-you-go lets a new customer provision a paid organization without a fixed subscription commitment
Three environment types let teams size API runtime capability to the deployment rather than use one environment class for every workload
Google Cloud billing and Metrics Explorer expose the resources that drive environment, API-call, and deployment-unit charges
cons: There is no single published total price because environments, API calls, proxy deployment units, regions, and network transfer can all affect cost
Unsuccessful API calls are still processed and included in the billable API-call count
The free evaluation is time-limited, does not support production workloads, and is not covered by Google support terms

faq.question: How is Apigee pay-as-you-go priced?
faq.answer: Google Cloud documents three core meters: active environments per region, API calls to deployed proxies, and proxy deployment units used per hour and region. Network charges can also apply.

faq.question: Are failed API calls billable in Apigee?
faq.answer: Yes. Apigee’s pay-as-you-go FAQ states that successful and unsuccessful requests are processed by the runtime and included in the API-call count.

faq.question: Can Apigee be evaluated for free?
faq.answer: A time-limited evaluation organization is available for new customers, but Google says it is not for production workloads and is not covered by Google support terms.
